title: Blood Orange Marmalade
subtitle: Deep crimson marmalade with a less bitter, sweeter flavour than Seville
excerpt: Blood oranges give a dramatic dark-red marmalade with a sweeter, less aggressively bitter character than Seville orange. Available from December through March. Makes about four 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Pam Corbin, Preserves. Blood oranges have moderate pectin, lower than Seville, so added lemon juice helps the set.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare and soak the peel the evening before the cooking day.

glossaryTerms.definition: 105 °C for marmalade; higher than jam. Confirmed by the wrinkle test on a chilled plate.

content.text: Blood orange marmalade has a striking deep crimson colour and a character quite different from Seville: sweeter, fruitier, with less of the medicinal bitterness. The colour holds better than you might expect in the jar,  a deep garnet rather than the vivid red of the fresh fruit. Makes about four 450 g jars.

Halve and juice the blood oranges. Reserve the juice. Scrape the pith and pips into a muslin square and tie into a bundle. Shred the peel into thin strips. Put the peel, muslin bundle, reserved juice, lemon juice, and water into the jam pan. Bring to a simmer and cook gently, covered, for 1 hour until the peel is completely tender.
Lift out and squeeze the muslin bundle. Add the sugar and stir over low heat until dissolved. Bring to a full rolling boil. Cook until the thermometer reads 105 (the
) °C, usually 15 to 20 minutes. Test on a cold plate. When the surface wrinkles, take off the heat, skim, rest 10 minutes, stir to distribute peel, then jar and seal.

items.cause: Blood orange colour is sensitive to prolonged heat.
items.fix: A hard, fast boil, not a slow simmer, to setting point preserves colour better. Don't extend cooking beyond what's needed to reach 105 °C.

items.cause: Blood oranges have more sugar than Seville.
items.fix: Reduce sugar to 1.3 kg and increase lemon juice to 80 ml next time.

items.cause: Not simmered long enough before sugar went in.
items.fix: The peel must be completely soft, collapsing when pressed. Blood orange peel takes 45 to 60 minutes minimum to soften.

items.cause: Blood oranges have lower pectin than Seville.
items.fix: Return to the pan, add 2 more tbsp lemon juice, reach 105 °C on the thermometer, and test again.
